applications.description: Change of Use of Existing Residential Care Home buildings and post office to 5 Private Dwellings, including demolitions and alterations

conditions.summary: Commencement within three years
conditions.text: The development shall be begun before the expiration of three years from the date of this permission.

conditions.summary: Accordance with approved plans
conditions.text: The development hereby permitted shall not be carried out except in complete accordance with the details shown on the submitted plans: Site Location Plan, GH-24-13 Proposed Elevations, GH-24-11 Proposed Floor Plans, GH-24-10A Parking Plan

conditions.summary: Materials as specified in application
conditions.text: The development shall be carried out using the materials as specified within the application.

conditions.summary: Boundary treatment approval prior to occupation
conditions.text: Before the first occupation of any dwelling hereby approved, details of all boundary treatment shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. Development shall be carried out in accordance with these approved details prior to the first occupation of the dwelling to which the details relate and shall thereafter be so retained.

conditions.summary: Tree protection in accordance with BS5837:2012
conditions.text: No development shall take place until all trees to be retained have been protected in accordance with BS5837:2012. The protective measures shall be retained throughout the duration of demolition, building and engineering works in the vicinity of the trees to be protected. Within the Construction Exclusion Zone, the existing ground level shall be neither raised nor lowered, and no materials or temporary building or surplus soil shall be placed or stored there. If any trenches for services are required, they shall be excavated and backfilled by hand and any tree roots encountered with a diameter of 5cm or more shall be left unsevered.

conditions.summary: Landscaping scheme submission and approval
conditions.text: No above ground development shall take place until there has been submitted to and approved, in writing, by the Local Planning Authority a scheme of hard and soft landscaping works for the site, which shall include any proposed changes in ground levels and also accurately identify spread, girth and species of all existing trees, shrubs and hedgerows on the site and indicate any to be retained.

conditions.summary: Landscaping implementation and maintenance
conditions.text: All changes in ground levels, hard landscaping, planting, seeding or turfing shown on the approved landscaping details shall be carried out during the first planting and seeding season (October - March inclusive) following the commencement of the development or in such other phased arrangement as may be agreed in writing by the Local Planning Authority. Any trees or shrubs which, within a period of 5 years of being planted die are removed or seriously damaged or seriously diseased shall be replaced in the next planting season with others of similar size and species.

conditions.summary: Ecological mitigation measures from Updated Ecology Survey
conditions.text: The development shall be carried out in accordance with the mitigation measures set out in Updated Ecology Survey 3rd June 2024.

conditions.summary: Obscure glazing for Unit 1 bedroom window
conditions.text: Notwithstanding the provisions of Article 3, Schedule 2, Part 1 of the Town and Country Planning (General Permitted Development) Order (England) 2015 (or any Order revoking and re-enacting that Order with or without modification), the side facing bedroom window serving Unit 1 on the approved plan shall be glazed in obscure glass to a level equivalent to Pilkington Level 3 or above before the dwelling hereby permitted is first occupied and shall thereafter be permanently retained in this approved form.

conditions.summary: Restriction on permitted development rights
conditions.text: Notwithstanding the provisions of Article 3, Schedule 2, Part 1 Classes A-E of the Town and Country Planning (General Permitted Development) (England) Order (or any Order revoking and re-enacting that Order with or without modification), no enlargement, improvement or other alteration to the dwelling, and no provision of buildings, enclosures, swimming or other pool, shall be erected or carried out except with prior planning permission.

conditions.summary: Flood risk mitigation measures and doorway protection
conditions.text: The development hereby approved shall be carried out in accordance with the mitigation measures as set out in the Michael Evans Flood Risk Assessment 14/03/2024 prior to the first occupation of any dwelling hereby approved. This shall include doorway flood protection for plots 4 and 5.

conditions.summary: External lighting details approval prior to occupation
conditions.text: Before the first occupation of any dwelling hereby approved, details of external lighting on the building and within the grounds, shall be submitted and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. Development shall be carried out in accordance with these approved details.

conditions.summary: Access widening to 5m prior to occupation
conditions.text: The access shall be widened to 5m as shown on the approved plan GH-24-10A prior to the first occupation of any dwelling hereby approved and shall thereafter be retained in accordance with the approved plan.

conditions.summary: Car parking and turning provision and retention
conditions.text: Car parking and turning shall be provided in accordance with plan GH-24-10A prior to the first occupation of any dwelling hereby approved and shall thereafter be retained in perpetuity and not used for any other purpose other than the parking and turning of vehicles.

conditions.summary: Surface water drainage at access prior to occupation
conditions.text: The existing access and extension thereof must incorporate a method of surface water drainage to ensure that no private surface water can flow on to the public highway prior to the first occupation of any dwelling hereby approved and shall thereafter be so maintained.

conditions.summary: Construction Management Plan submission and approval
conditions.text: No development shall take place, including any demolition work, until a Construction Management Plan has been submitted and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority, which will include the following:- a) A scheme for monitoring, reporting and control of construction noise and vibration including hours of working and scope for remedial action; b) A scheme for the control of dust and scope for remedial action in the event that dust is identified as an issue or any complaints are received; c) Details of a chassis and wheel cleaning system to be used for all construction vehicles leaving the site; d) Haul routes to the site and hours of delivery; e) Measures to ensure that vehicles entering the site can do so immediately upon arrival; f) Details to ensure that any parking, waiting, loading/unloading only occurs in the marked out parking bay directly adjacent to the site; g) Details of any events that is likely to require a banksman for larger vehicles to reverse in to the site and methodology; h) Details of site compounds, storage area and contractor/visitor parking/turning; i) Details of the site enclosure or part thereof and gated site security; j) Confirmation that any demolition will be carried out in accordance with the ecological assessment; k) Details of site notice with contact details and a scheme for dealing with complaints; l) Details of any temporary lighting which must not directly light the public highway; m) A scheme for recycling/disposing of waste resulting from the demolition and construction works; n) The erection and maintenance of security hoarding including decorative displays and facilities for public viewing, where appropriate. The development shall thereafter be carried out in accordance with the approved Construction Management Plan.

applications.address: Land To The South Of Pilton Village Luffenham Lane Pilton Rutland
applications.description: Full Planning Application for the installation and operation of a solar farm together with all associated works, equipment, necessary infrastructure and biodiversity enhancement areas.

conditions.summary: Commencement within three years
conditions.text: The development shall be begun before the expiration of three years from the date of this permission.

conditions.summary: Accordance with approved plans and documents
conditions.text: The development hereby permitted shall be carried out in accordance with the details shown in the following approved documents and plans: Site Location Plan drawing number P22_1447_EN_09D Sheet 1 - 4 dated 09/01/2024; Detailed Landscape Proposals drawing number P22-1447_EN_0001_S1 to S5 Revision C dated 22/11/2023; Site Layout drawing number BSE256-SD-01 Revision 08 dated 04.09.2023; [and other specified drawings and documents as listed].

conditions.summary: Finish and colour of structures and equipment approval
conditions.text: Notwithstanding any details submitted, no development shall commence on site until full details of the finish and colour of all structures, equipment, fencing and support frames for the solar panels hereby approved have been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. Development shall be carried out in accordance with the approved details and maintained thereafter for the lifetime of the development hereby approved.

conditions.summary: 40-year operational period and decommissioning
conditions.text: Within 1 month of the date of first export of electricity to either the National Grid or to the Wing Water Treatment Works ('the date of first export') confirmation shall be provided in writing to the Local Planning Authority of the same. The use of the land for the generation of electricity as hereby permitted shall cease on or before the expiry of a 40-year period from the date of first export. The land shall thereafter be restored to its former condition in accordance with a scheme of decommissioning work ('Decommissioning Method Statement'). The Decommissioning Method Statement, including the dismantling and removal of all elements (with the exception of the Substation and associated access), shall be submitted to the Local Planning Authority for approval not later than 39 years and 6 months from the date of first export of electricity, or within 3 months of the cessation of electricity generation at the site, whichever is earlier.

conditions.summary: Tree and hedgerow protection during construction and decommissioning
conditions.text: Before any works commence on site other than site preparation works, the trees and hedgerows shown for retention on Plan BHA_4736_02 shall be protected as required in accordance with BS5837 and that plan and shall remain so protected until all construction on site is complete. The trees shall be protected during the decommissioning of the site in the same manner or in accordance with any standard that subsequently supersedes BS5837.

conditions.summary: Landscaping implementation and maintenance
conditions.text: All changes in hard landscaping, planting, seeding or turfing shown on the approved landscaping details shall be carried out during the first planting and seeding season (October - March inclusive) following the commencement of the development or in such other phased arrangement as may be agreed in writing by the Local Planning Authority. Any trees or shrubs which, within a period of 5 years of being planted die are removed or seriously damaged or seriously diseased shall be replaced in the next planting season with others of similar size and species.

conditions.summary: Noise impact assessment (BS4142:2014+A1:2019)
conditions.text: A noise impact assessment shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The assessment shall be undertaken in accordance with BS 4142:2014+A1(2019) prior to commencement, taking into account both day and night-time noise levels, and will be used to inform any necessary noise mitigation scheme for the proposed development. Thereafter the development shall be implemented in accordance with the approved details, including any necessary mitigation, prior to first use, and shall thereafter be retained and maintained as such in perpetuity.

conditions.summary: Contaminated land risk assessment and remediation
conditions.text: No development other than that required to be carried out as part of an approved scheme of remediation shall commence until sections (i) to (iii) of this condition, below, have been complied with. If unexpected contamination is found after development has begun, development shall be halted on that part of the site affected by the unexpected contamination to the extent specified by the Local Planning Authority in writing until section (iv) has been complied with in relation to that contamination. [Detailed subsections for Site Characterisation, Submission of Remediation Scheme, Implementation of Approved Remediation Scheme, and Reporting of Unexpected Contamination as specified in the notice].

conditions.summary: Soil Management Plan for construction, operation and decommissioning
conditions.text: Prior to the commencement of each phase of development (Construction, Operation and Decommissioning), a Soil Management Plan shall be submitted to, and approved in writing by, the Local Planning Authority. The plan shall include, but not be limited to details pertaining to careful soil management during each phase, including consideration of the appropriate time of year for soil handling, planting beneath the panels and returning the land to the former land quality as indicated in Appendix 6 of the Agricultural Land Classification survey dated 3rd March 2023.

conditions.summary: Access implementation on Morcott Road
conditions.text: Prior to the installation of the solar panel infrastructure for each phase the related access on Morcott Road shall be fully implemented in accordance with the details shown on the Proposed Access Arrangements plan ref P22-1447-Figure 3.1.

conditions.summary: Internal access roads, parking and turning facilities
conditions.text: Prior to commissioning the solar farm infrastructure, the facilities for internal access roads, parking and turning shall be fully implemented, with full details to be submitted to the Local Planning Authority for approval in writing prior to commencement. Following any wholesale solar panel replacement scheme, any damaged areas or routes will be fully remediated.

conditions.summary: Vehicle-to-vehicle visibility splays
conditions.text: Prior to commencement of development vehicle to vehicle visibility splays will be provided in accordance with the details shown on the Proposed Access Arrangements plan, ref P22-1447-Figure 3.1, with no obstruction above 600mm above ground level and thereafter maintained until the completion of decommissioning the site.

conditions.summary: Construction vehicle routing via approved green route
conditions.text: All construction vehicles associated with the solar panel areas and access via Morcott Road will use the green construction route only as shown on the Construction Traffic Routing Plan, ref P22-1447 Figure 4.1, which applies to the construction, any wholesale replacement scheme and decommissioning.

conditions.summary: Construction Management Plan requirements
conditions.text: No development shall take place until a Construction Management Plan has been submitted and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority, which will include the following:- a) A scheme for monitoring, reporting and control of construction noise and vibration including hours of working and scope for remedial action; b) A scheme for the control of dust and scope for remedial action; c) A scheme of chassis and wheel cleaning for all construction vehicles; d) Measures to ensure that vehicles can access the site immediately upon arrival; e) Details of site compounds, storage area and contractor/visitor parking/turning; f) Details of the site enclosure or part thereof and gated site security; g) Confirmation of any tree protection measures; h) Details of site notice with contact details and complaints scheme; i) Details of any temporary lighting which must not directly light the public highway; j) Phasing plans where necessary; k) A scheme for recycling/disposing of waste resulting from the construction works; l) The erection and maintenance of security hoarding including decorative displays.

conditions.summary: Temporary facilities for construction vehicle parking and turning
conditions.text: Temporary facilities for the internal access roads, parking, turning, loading and unloading of all vehicles visiting the site during the construction period shall be provided prior to installation of any solar panel infrastructure, prior to any wholesale solar panel replacement scheme and prior to the decommissioning period, in accordance with the details approved as part of the Construction Management Plan.

conditions.summary: Private lighting arrangements for highway safety
conditions.text: Any private temporary or permanent lighting shall be arranged so that no danger or inconvenience is caused to users of the public highway.

conditions.summary: Pre and post-construction photographic highway surveys
conditions.text: Prior to the commencement of any work on the site, a photographic survey will be carried out of The Cock Pit, Back Lane (between The Cock Pit and Wing Road), Wing Road (between Back Lane and Morcott Road), and Morcott Road (between Wing Road and 50m north of Pinfold Lane) and submitted to the Local Planning Authority. A replica photographic survey will be carried out within one month of the completion of construction to identify any damage to the highway resulting from traffic movements associated with the development and submitted to the Local Planning Authority. Any identified damage will need to be remediated by the applicant within three months of the date of that survey.

conditions.summary: Biodiversity Enhancement and Management Plan implementation
conditions.text: The development shall be undertaken in accordance with the Biodiversity Enhancement and Management Plan (prepared by Avian Ecology, dated May 2024) the updated Appendix 2 section 7, submitted to the Local Planning Authority on 11th July 2024, the Biodiversity Net Gain Assessment (prepared by Avian Ecology, dated 1st May 2024) and Landscape and Ecological Management Plan (prepared by Pegasus Group, dated 1st February 2024).

conditions.summary: Construction Method Statement for surface water control
conditions.text: No development shall take place until a Construction Method Statement has been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority which shall detail measures for the control of surface water drainage during the construction stage of the proposed development. It shall include details for the methodology and measures to be put in place to ensure no flooding from the site and how those measures will be managed. The approved Construction Method Statement shall thereafter be strictly adhered to throughout the construction period.

conditions.summary: Secondary Construction Method Statement for wholesale replacement
conditions.text: No wholesale replacement shall take place until a Secondary Construction Method Statement has been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority which shall detail measures for the control of surface water drainage during the construction stage of the proposed development. No works nor delivers shall take place outside of these time without the prior written agreement of the Local Planning Authority.

conditions.summary: Construction Management Plan with noise, dust, hours and traffic controls
conditions.text: No development shall take place, including any demolition work, until a Construction Management Plan has been submitted and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority, which will include the following:- a. A scheme for monitoring, reporting and control of construction noise and vibration including hours of working and scope for remedial action. b. A scheme for the control of dust and scope for remedial action in the event that dust is identified as an issue or any complaints are received. c. Haul routes to the site from the strategic road network and hours of delivery d. Measures to ensure that vehicles can access the site immediately upon arrival to ensure there is no park, waiting, loading/unloading or queuing on the public highway. e. Details of site compounds, storage area and contractor/visitor parking/turning. f. Details of the site enclosure or part thereof and gated site security. g. Confirmation that any demolition will be carried out in accordance with the ecological assessment. h. Details of site notice with contact details and a scheme for dealing with complaints. i. Details of any temporary lighting which must not directly light the public highway. j. A scheme for recycling/disposing of waste resulting from the demolition and construction works. k. The erection and maintenance of security hoarding including decorative displays and facilities for public viewing, where appropriate.

conditions.summary: 30 year Habitat Monitoring and Management Plan for biodiversity gain
conditions.text: The development shall not commence until a 30 year Habitat Monitoring and Management Plan (HMMP), prepared in accordance with an approved Biodiversity Gain Plan, has been submitted to and approved in writing by the local planning authority. The approved HMMP shall be strictly adhered to and implemented in full for its duration and shall contain the following: a) Description and evaluation of the features to be managed; b) Ecological trends and constraints on site that may influence management; c) Aims, objectives and targets for management - links with local and national species and habitat action plans; d) Description of the management operations necessary to achieving aims and objectives; e) Preparation of a works schedule, including annual works schedule; f) Details and a timetable of the monitoring needed to measure the effectiveness of management; g) Details of the persons responsible for the implementation and monitoring; h) Mechanisms of adaptive management to account for necessary changes in work schedule to achieve the required targets; and i) Details of methodology and frequency of monitoring reports to be submitted to the Local Planning Authority to assess biodiversity gain

conditions.summary: Public Right of Way (PROW) Operational Safety Plan
conditions.text: Prior to the first occupation or use of the development, a Public Right of Way (PROW) Operational Safety Plan shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The Plan shall include: An assessment of the operational phase risks to users of Public Footpath E227 arising from vehicle and pedestrian movements within the site following completion of the development; Details of the permanent measures to manage pedestrian/vehicle interaction, including routing, surface markings, lining, signage and visibility improvements; Arrangements for the future monitoring, maintenance and upgrading of the measures where required to ensure continued safe operation for the lifetime of the development. The development shall thereafter operate only in accordance with the approved PROW Operational Safety Plan.

conditions.text: All areas of hedges, scrub or similar vegetation where birds may nest which are to be removed as part of the development, are to be cleared outside the bird-nesting season (March - August inclusive) or if clearance during the bird nesting season cannot be reasonably be avoided, a suitably qualified ecologist will check the areas to be removed immediately prior to clearance and advise whether nesting birds are present. If active nests are recorded, no vegetation clearance or other works that may disturb active nests shall proceed until all young have fledged the nest.

conditions.summary: Habitat management and ecological enhancements (BNG)
conditions.text: The recommended habitat management and ecological enhancements set out within the Ecological Assessment and Biodiversity Net Gain Plan by EPR dated August 2023 ref. 22/86-3B shall be implemented and permanently maintained in accordance with the approved details.

applications.address: Abbeyfield 2 Pound Avenue Stevenage Herts SG1 3JA
applications.description: Demolition of existing care home and erection of 15 no. flats, extended dropped kerb, associated parking and ancillary works

conditions.summary: Development in accordance with approved plans
conditions.text: The development hereby permitted shall be carried out in accordance with the following approved plans: 23069-0000-P1; 23069-0100-P1; 23069-0101-P1; ASC.23.521; 23069-0300-P1; 23069-1103-P2; 23069-1100-P3; 23069-1101-P2; 23069-1102-P2; 23069-1300-P4;

conditions.summary: Development to commence within 3 years
conditions.text: The development hereby permitted shall be begun before the expiration of three years from the date of this permission.

conditions.summary: Construction hours and deliveries
conditions.text: No demolition, construction or maintenance activities audible at the boundary, and no deliveries of construction and demolition materials shall be undertaken outside the hours 07:30 hours to 18:00 hours Monday to Friday and 08:00 hours to 13:00 hours on Saturdays. For the avoidance of doubt, no such activity shall take place on Sundays or Bank Holidays, unless otherwise agreed in writing with the Local Planning Authority.

conditions.summary: External lighting to avoid spillage beyond site boundaries
conditions.text: Any external lighting installed at the site shall be angled so as to avoid any spillage beyond the site boundaries unless otherwise agreed in writing by the Local Planning Authority.

conditions.summary: Contaminated land - unexpected contamination procedure
conditions.text: In the event that contamination is found at any time when carrying out the approved development that was not previously identified, it must be reported in writing immediately to the local planning authority. An investigation and risk assessment must be undertaken and where remediation is necessary, a remediation scheme must be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. Following completion of measures identified in the approved remediation scheme, a verification report must be submitted to and approved in writing by the local planning authority.

conditions.summary: Replacement of dead or damaged trees within 5 years
conditions.text: Any trees or plants comprised within the scheme of landscaping, which within a period of five years from the completion of the development die, are removed or become seriously damaged or diseased shall be replaced in the next planting season with others of similar size and species, unless otherwise agreed in writing by the Local Planning Authority.

conditions.summary: Landscaping planting to be carried out in first planting season
conditions.text: All planting, seeding or turfing comprised in the approved details of landscaping shall be carried out in the first planting and seeding seasons following the first occupation of the building(s) or the completion of the development whichever is the sooner.

conditions.summary: Noise Impact Assessment compliance
conditions.text: The development hereby approved shall be carried out in accordance with the Noise Impact Assessment prepared by IEC Limited, reference IEC/4552/01/AVH dated 08.12.2023 and subsequent Technical Note reference IEC001 dated 01.08.2024 unless otherwise agreed in writing by the Local Planning Authority.

conditions.summary: Ground floor units to be Category 2 accessible and adaptable dwellings
conditions.text: The ground floor residential units should all be Category 2: Accessible and Adaptable dwellings.

conditions.summary: Minimum Finished Floor Level for flood resistance (90.9 mAOD)
conditions.text: The development will be constructed as per the approved documents including the minimum Finished Floor Level (FFL) of 90.9 mAOD. This is to ensure that the development should be appropriately flood resistant and resilient such that, in the event of a flood, it could be quickly brought back into use without significant refurbishment.

conditions.summary: First floor eastern windows to be obscured and restricted opening
conditions.text: The first floor windows in the eastern side elevation of the development hereby approved shall be glazed with obscured glass and shall be fixed so as to be incapable of being opened below a height of 1.7 metres above floor level, and shall be retained in that form thereafter.

conditions.summary: Construction Management Plan required
conditions.text: No development shall commence until a Construction Management Plan has been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority in consultation with the Highway Authority. Thereafter the construction of the development shall only be carried out in accordance with the approved Plan. The Plan would need to include details of: a. Construction vehicle numbers, type, routing; b. Access arrangements to the site; c. Traffic management requirements; d. Construction and storage compounds (including areas designated for car parking); e. Siting and details of wheel washing facilities; f. Cleaning of site entrances, site tracks and the adjacent public highway; g. Timing of construction activities including delivery times and removal of waste, and to avoid school pick up/drop off times. h. Provision of sufficient on-site parking prior to commencement of construction activities; i. Post construction restoration/reinstatement of the working areas and temporary access to the public highway; j. where works cannot be contained wholly within the site a plan should be submitted showing the site layout on the highway including extent of hoarding, pedestrian routes and remaining road width for vehicle movements; k. Phasing Plan.

conditions.summary: Tree protection measures for trees to be retained
conditions.text: No development shall take place (including site clearance and demolition) until details of tree protection measures for the trees to the south of the application site and any trees on the site have been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The tree protection measures as approved shall be implemented prior to commencement of development and remain in place until the development has been completed. Within the tree protection areas to be fenced off there shall be no alteration to the ground level and they shall be kept clear of vehicles, materials, surplus soil, temporary buildings, plant and machinery.

conditions.summary: Site Waste Management Plan required
conditions.text: No development shall take place (including site clearance and demolition) until a Site Waste Management Plan (SWMP) for the site has been submitted to the Local Planning Authority and approved in consultation with the Waste Planning Authority. The SWMP should aim to reduce the amount of waste produced on site and should contain information including estimated types and quantities of waste to arise from construction and waste management actions for each waste type. The development shall be carried out in accordance with the approved SWMP.

conditions.summary: Surface water drainage construction drawings and method statement
conditions.text: Prior to the commencement of development, construction drawings of the surface water drainage network, associated sustainable drainage components and flow control mechanisms and a construction method statement shall be submitted and agreed in writing by the local planning authority. The scheme shall then be constructed as per the agreed drawings, method statement, Drainage Strategy and Drawings (Drainage Strategy and Drawing Rev P6, dated 15 December 2025) and remaining in perpetuity for the lifetime of the development unless agreed in writing by the Local Planning Authority. No alteration to the agreed drainage scheme shall occur without prior written approval from the Local Authority.

conditions.summary: Schedule and samples of external materials
conditions.text: No development shall take place above slab level until a schedule and samples of the materials to be used in the construction of the external surfaces of the development hereby permitted have been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. Development shall be carried out in accordance with the approved details.

conditions.summary: Climate change adaptation measures
conditions.text: No development shall take place above slab level until details of measures to address adaptation to climate change have been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. These measures shall then be implemented and permanently maintained in accordance with the approved details.

conditions.summary: Boundary treatment details
conditions.text: No development shall take place above slab level until details of the treatment of all boundaries including details of any walls, fences, gates or other means of enclosure shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority prior to the commencement of development. The approved boundary treatments shall be completed before the use hereby permitted is commenced or before the building(s) is occupied.

conditions.summary: Soft and hard landscaping scheme
conditions.text: No development shall take place above slab level until there has been submitted to and approved by the Local Planning Authority a scheme of soft and hard landscaping and details of the treatment of all hard surfaces. The scheme shall include details of all existing trees and hedgerows on the land and details showing all trees to be removed, or retained, together with details of all new planting to take place including species, size and method of planting.

conditions.summary: Water supplies and fire hydrants provision
conditions.text: No development shall take place above slab level until a scheme for the provision of adequate water supplies and fire hydrants, necessary for firefighting purposes at the site, has been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The development shall not be occupied until the scheme has been implemented in accordance with the approved details.

conditions.summary: Integrated swift bricks and bat boxes
conditions.text: No development shall take place above slab level until details of integrated swift bricks and bat boxes to be provided within the development have been submitted to and approved in writing by the local planning authority. The development shall then be carried out in accordance with the approved details.

conditions.summary: Parking provision with porous materials or SuDS
conditions.text: Prior to the first occupation of the dwellings herby permitted the parking provision as shown on the approved plans, shall be constructed, hardsurfaced and made ready for use. Any new areas of hardstanding created, or existing areas which are replaced, shall be constructed in a porous material or provision shall be made for a sustainable urban drainage system (SuDS) to be built into the hardsurfaced areas. Once provided the parking facilities shall be retained in that form and thereafter be used for the parking of vehicles only.

conditions.summary: Electric vehicle charging point infrastructure
conditions.text: Prior to the first occupation of the dwellings hereby permitted, all parking spaces shall be provided with the underlying infrastructure for connection to the electricity network to enable them to be served by an electric vehicle charging point.

conditions.summary: Cycle storage provision (20 cycles minimum)
conditions.text: Prior to the first occupation of the dwellings hereby permitted, the cycle storage as shown on approved plan 23069-1100-P3, for the storage of not less than 20 cycles in a single storey formation shall be implemented accordingly. The cycle storage shall be retained and maintained accordingly during the lifetime of the development.

conditions.summary: Waste and recycling storage area
conditions.text: Prior to the first occupation of the dwellings hereby permitted, the waste and recycling storage area as shown on plan 23069-1100-P3 shall be implemented accordingly. The storage shall be retained and maintained accordingly during the lifetime of the development.

conditions.summary: SuDS maintenance and management plan
conditions.text: The development hereby approved shall not be occupied until details of the maintenance and management of the sustainable drainage scheme have been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The drainage scheme shall be implemented prior to the first occupation of the development hereby approved and thereafter managed and maintained in accordance with the approved details in perpetuity. The Local Planning Authority shall be granted access to inspect the sustainable drainage scheme for the lifetime of the development. The details of the scheme to be submitted for approval shall include: i. a timetable for its implementation. ii. details of SuDS feature and connecting drainage structures and maintenance requirement for each aspect including a drawing showing where they are located. iii. a management and maintenance plan for the lifetime of the development which shall include the arrangements for adoption by any public body or statutory undertaker, or any other arrangements to secure the operation of the sustainable drainage scheme throughout its lifetime. This will include the name and contact details of any appointed management company.

conditions.summary: Surface water drainage survey and verification report
conditions.text: Upon completion of the surface water drainage system, including any SuDS features, and prior to the first use of the development; a survey and verification report from an independent surveyor shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The survey and report shall demonstrate that the surface water drainage system has been constructed in accordance with the details approved pursuant to condition 15. Where necessary, details of corrective works to be carried out along with a timetable for their completion, shall be included for approval in writing by the Local Planning Authority. Any corrective works required shall be carried out in accordance with the approved timetable and subsequently re-surveyed with the findings submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority.

conditions.text: The development hereby permitted shall be carried out in accordance with the following approved plans: Site Location Plan; Existing Floor Plan;

conditions.summary: Commencement within three years
conditions.text: The development hereby permitted shall be begun before the expiration of three years from the date of this permission.

conditions.summary: Use restriction to supported living care home for adults aged 18-64, maximum 3 residents
conditions.text: The premises shall be used for a residential care home for adults aged 18 to 64, and for no other purpose, including any other purpose in Use Class C2 of the Schedule to the Town and Country Planning (Use Classes) Order 1987 (as amended) or in any provision equivalent to that Class in any statutory instrument revoking or re-enacting that order with or without modification. The number of adults cared for and resident on the premises shall not exceed three at any one time.

conditions.summary: Construction hours restriction (Monday-Friday 07:30-18:00, Saturday 08:00-13:00, no Sundays/Bank Holidays)
conditions.text: No demolition or construction work relating to this permission, audible at the site boundary, shall be carried out on any Sunday, Public or Bank Holiday nor at any other time, except between the hours of 07:30am and 18:00pm on Mondays to Fridays and between the hours of 08:00am and 13:00pm on Saturdays.

conditions.summary: Commencement within three years

conditions.summary: Restriction of use to children's care home (4 children maximum)
conditions.text: The premises shall be used for a residential children's care home and for no other purpose, including any other purpose in Use Class C2 of the Schedule to the Town and Country Planning (Use Classes) Order 1987 (as amended) or in any provision equivalent to that Class in any statutory instrument revoking or re-enacting that order with or without modification. The number of children cared for and resident on the premises shall not exceed four at any one time.

conditions.summary: Development to commence within 3 years
conditions.text: The development hereby permitted shall be begun before the expiration of three years from the date of this permission.

conditions.summary: Implementation of Ecological Impact Assessment recommendations
conditions.text: The recommendations set out within the Ecological Impact Assessment by The Environment Partnership dated April 2025 shall be implemented and permanently maintained in accordance with the approved details.

conditions.summary: Protection of retained trees for 5 years post-completion
conditions.text: No tree shown retained on the approved plans, or subsequently approved landscaping scheme, shall be cut down, uprooted or destroyed, nor shall any retained tree be topped or lopped within five years of the completion of development without the written approval of the Local Planning Authority.

conditions.summary: Replacement of trees lost within 5 years post-completion
conditions.text: If any retained tree referred to in condition 4 is removed, uprooted or destroyed or dies within 5 years of the completion of development, a replacement tree should be planted in the same place.

conditions.summary: Site contamination remediation and verification report
conditions.text: The site contamination remediation measures set out within Section 10.0 of the Phase 2 Site Investigation Report Entrance Building Extension to Lister Hospital, Stevenage by Clancy Consulting (ref 10/2450/002 Rev 02) shall be implemented in full. A verification report shall be submitted to and approved by the Local Planning Authority, upon completion of the remedial measures.

conditions.summary: Replacement of failed or damaged landscape planting within 5 years
conditions.text: Any trees or plants comprised within the scheme of landscaping, which within a period of five years from the completion of the development die, are removed or become seriously damaged or diseased shall be replaced in the next planting season with others of similar size and species, unless otherwise agreed in writing by the Local Planning Authority.

conditions.text: The development hereby permitted shall be carried out in accordance with the following approved plans: 01 Rev A; 02 Rev A; Battery Box Rev A; 04 Rev B;

conditions.summary: Commencement within three years
conditions.text: The development hereby permitted shall be begun before the expiration of three years from the date of this permission.

conditions.summary: External materials in accordance with approved plans
conditions.text: The external materials used in the development to which this permission relates shall be those detailed on the approved plans and in the accompanying planning submission documents unless otherwise agreed in writing by the local planning authority.

applications.address: Brogdale Farm Brogdale Road Ospringe ME13 8XU
applications.description: Outline planning application for mixed-use development comprising up to 360sqm nursery school (use Class Ef), up to five holiday lets and up to 1,710sqm of flexible workshop, industrial & research and development floorspace (use Class Eg (ii, iii), with all matters reserved except access from Brogdale Road.

applications.address: Sittingbourne Logistics Park Swale Way Sittingbourne Kent ME10 2FF
applications.description: Outline application (all matters reserved except for access) for erection of up to 2,800m2 of additional storage and distribution (B8 use) warehouse floorspace and HGV parking including access, parking, landscaping and other associated works.

conditions.summary: Reserved matters approval for appearance, landscaping, layout and scale
conditions.text: Details relating to the appearance, landscaping, layout and scale of the proposed development shall be submitted to and approved by the Local Planning Authority for each phase of development, before the development of that phase is commenced.

conditions.summary: First reserved matters application deadline (3 years)
conditions.text: The first application for approval of reserved matters referred to in condition (1) must be made to the Local Planning Authority no later than the expiration of three years beginning with the date of the grant of outline planning permission.

conditions.summary: First phase commencement deadline (2 years from reserved matters approval)
conditions.text: The first phase of development to which this permission relates must be begun no later than the expiration of two years from the final approval of the relevant reserved matters.

conditions.summary: Development in accordance with approved drawings and documents
conditions.text: The development hereby permitted shall be carried out in accordance with the following approved drawings and documents: Site Plan and Initial Works Area (ecology) ref. 0871_DR09; Parameter Plan ref. 60472599_ACM_XX_XX_DR_CE_1018; Phasing Plan ref. 60472599_ACM_XX_XX_DR_CE_1009; Illustrative Masterplan ref. 60472599_ACM_XX_XX_DR_CE_1029; Proposed access arrangements ref. 109617-dwg-101-01 P5; Site Boundary Plan ref. 60472599_ACM_XX_XX_DR_CE_1010; Preliminary Levels drawing ref. 60472599_ACM_XX_XX_DR_CE_1014.

conditions.summary: Warehouse maximum height limit (12 metres)
conditions.text: The details submitted pursuant to condition 1 (reserved matters) shall demonstrate that the hereby approved warehouses shall be no more than 12 metres in height.

conditions.summary: Secured by Design principles including natural surveillance
conditions.text: The details submitted pursuant to condition (1) (the reserved matters) shall include details demonstrating how the development meets the principles of 'secured by design', particularly in relation to natural surveillance.

conditions.summary: BREEAM certification for non-residential buildings
conditions.text: Any reserved matters applications for non-residential buildings within the development hereby approved, shall be accompanied by evidence demonstrating that the development is registered with a BREEAM certification body and a pre-assessment report (or design stage certificate with interim rating if available). All non-residential buildings over 1000sqm gross floor area shall achieve a minimum final BREEAM level of 'very good' or equivalent as a minimum, with non-residential buildings under that threshold achieving 'good' or equivalent as a minimum. The pre-assessment report for each relevant building, shall be submitted and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. Any non-residential buildings shall not be first used until a final certificate certifying that BREEAM rating 'very good' (if over 1000sqm) or 'good' (if below 1000sqm) has been achieved for the building has been submitted and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority.

conditions.summary: Contaminated land risk assessment and remediation scheme
conditions.text: The development hereby permitted shall not be commenced until the following components of a scheme to deal with the risks associated with contamination of the site shall have been submitted to and approved, in writing, by the local planning authority: 1) A preliminary risk assessment; 2) A site investigation; 3) A remediation method statement (RMS) based on site investigation results; 4) A Closure Report upon completion of works. Any changes to these components require the express consent of the local planning authority. The scheme shall thereafter be implemented as approved.

conditions.summary: External lighting scheme (ILP Guidance Note 01/21)
conditions.text: No external lighting shall be installed until a detailed scheme of lighting has been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. This scheme shall take note of and refer to the Institute of ILP Guidance Note 01/21 The Reduction Of Obtrusive Light (and any subsequent revisions) and shall include a layout plan with beam orientation and a schedule of light equipment proposed (luminaire type; mounting height; aiming angles and luminaire profiles) and an ISO lux plan showing light spill. The scheme of lighting shall be installed, maintained and operated in accordance with the approved details.

conditions.summary: Development to comply with Noise Impact Assessment
conditions.text: The development hereby approved shall be carried out and operate in accordance with the details set out in Noise Impact Assessment (AECOM, dated 9th May 2022).

conditions.summary: Air Quality Assessment measures implementation
conditions.text: Prior to the first use of the warehouses hereby approved, the measures contained in Air Quality Assessment, shall be implemented in full accordance with the details contained therein.

conditions.summary: Archaeological field evaluation, safeguarding and recording
conditions.text: To assess and mitigate the impacts of development on significant archaeological remains: A) Prior to any development works the applicant (or their agents or successors in title) shall secure and have reported a programme of archaeological field evaluation works, in accordance with a specification and written timetable which has been submitted to and approved by the local planning authority. B) Following completion of archaeological evaluation works, no development shall take place until the applicant or their agents or successors in title, has secured the implementation of any safeguarding measures to ensure preservation in situ of important archaeological remains and/or further archaeological investigation and recording in accordance with a specification and timetable which has been submitted to and approved by the local planning authority. C) The archaeological safeguarding measures, investigation and recording shall be carried out in accordance with the agreed specification and timetable. D) Within 6 months of the completion of archaeological works a Post Excavation Assessment Report shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the local planning authority.

conditions.summary: Ecological mitigation strategy review and approval
conditions.text: Prior to the works hereby approved commencing (including vegetation clearance), a review and, where required, update of ecological mitigation strategy must be submitted to the LPA and approved in writing. The review works shall include preliminary ecological appraisal and recommended species surveys, overview of mitigation required, detailed methodology to implement the mitigation, timing of works, plans showing areas where mitigation will be implemented and retained areas, details of how retained areas will be protected during works, and details of who will implement works. The works must be implemented as approved.

conditions.summary: Habitat establishment and management plan
conditions.text: Prior to works commencing on site, a habitat establishment and management plan must be submitted to the LPA for written approval. The plan must include aims and objectives, details of habitats to be created/enhanced/managed, plans of proposed/enhanced/retained habitats, details of methodology to prepare land for habitat creation, details of management required, details of ongoing management, and details of monitoring and management plan reviews. The plan must be implemented as approved.

conditions.summary: Site-wide lighting plan to protect retained habitats
conditions.text: Prior to the site being operational and prior to the first occupation of the development hereby approved, a site-wide lighting plan must be submitted to the Local Planning Authority for written approval. The plan must include details of anticipated vertical and horizontal light spill and demonstrate that the lighting will not impact retained habitats. The plan must be implemented as approved.

conditions.summary: Water vole and reptile mitigation implementation
conditions.text: No works shall commence (other than within the areas of existing hardstanding or areas where access work has been implemented) unless and until the water vole/reptile mitigation has been fully implemented, as set out and approved in the Ecological Impact Assessment and/or pursuant to condition 17.

conditions.summary: Water vole mitigation strategy for access road
conditions.text: Prior to any works on the access road commencing, a water vole mitigation strategy must be submitted to the Local Planning Authority for written approval. The strategy must be informed by a current water vole survey and demonstrate how the vegetation within the site will be cleared to avoid impacting water vole. The plan must be implemented as approved.

conditions.summary: Rainwater harvesting system details
conditions.text: Prior to the commencement of the development hereby approved, details of the rainwater harvesting system, including measures to prevent contamination of the water supply and any discharge to public sewers, and maintenance responsibilities and regimes for the rainwater harvesting system, shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority.

conditions.summary: Detailed sustainable surface water drainage scheme
conditions.text: No development shall begin in any phase until a detailed sustainable surface water drainage scheme for the site has been submitted to (and approved in writing by) the local planning authority. The detailed drainage scheme shall be based upon the principles contained within the Surface and Foul Water Drainage Strategies (24th March 2022- Revision 00). The submission shall also demonstrate that the surface water generated by this development (for all rainfall durations and intensities up to and including the climate change adjusted critical 100 year storm) can be accommodated and disposed of without increase to flood risk on or off-site. The drainage scheme shall also demonstrate that silt and pollutants can be adequately managed and appropriate operational, maintenance and access requirements are considered. The drainage scheme shall be implemented in accordance with the approved details.

conditions.summary: Drainage Verification Report prior to building occupation
conditions.text: No building on any phase (or within an agreed implementation schedule) of the development hereby permitted shall be occupied until a Verification Report, pertaining to the surface water drainage system and prepared by a suitably competent person, has been submitted to and approved by the Local Planning Authority. The Report shall demonstrate that the drainage system constructed is consistent with that which was approved and shall contain information and evidence of details and locations of inlets, outlets and control structures, landscape plans, full as built drawings, and an operation and maintenance manual for the sustainable drainage scheme as constructed.

conditions.summary: Construction Programme approval by Local Highways Authority
conditions.text: No part of the development shall commence until a Construction Programme has been submitted to and agreed upon in writing by the Local Highways Authority before any development commences on site.

conditions.summary: Construction Management Plan including vehicle routing and timing
conditions.text: No development shall commence on site until and unless the Construction Management Plan has been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The CMP shall include: (a) Routing of construction and delivery vehicles to / from site; (b) Parking and turning areas for construction and delivery vehicles and site personnel; (c) Timing of deliveries; (d) Provision of wheel washing facilities; (e) Temporary traffic management / signage. The development shall then be carried out in accordance with the agreed Construction Traffic Management Plan.

conditions.summary: Access implementation and maintenance
conditions.text: Prior to the first use of the site commencing, the access as shown on the submitted drawings shall be implemented and thereafter maintained.

conditions.summary: Visibility splays (1.2m obstruction limit)
conditions.text: Prior to the first use of the site commencing, visibility splays with no obstruction over 1.2 metres above carriageway level within the splays, shall be provided and thereafter maintained.

conditions.summary: Drainage location and prevention of surface water runoff to Strategic Road Network
conditions.text: Prior to the commencement of the development hereby approved, full details of new drainage and its location shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority (in consultation with National Highways). No surface water shall be permitted to run off from the development onto the Strategic Road Network or into any drainage system connected to the Strategic Road Network.

conditions.summary: Boundary treatment plan along A249 including tree management
conditions.text: Prior to any works being undertaken along the boundary with the A249, a boundary treatment plan shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority (in consultation with National Highways). The plan shall include details of fencing location, type, construction method and maintenance; details of management of existing boundary planting including an Arboricultural Tree Survey and Tree Protection Plan with a Method Statement for any works required to address the removal, retention and management of trees along this boundary. All works shall be undertaken in accordance with the agreed plan and maintained as such thereafter.

conditions.summary: Landscape Management Plan and Planting Schedule
conditions.text: Prior to the commencement of the development hereby permitted a Landscape Management Plan and Planting Schedule, and details of implementation and maintenance, shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority (in consultation with National Highways). Planting shall be undertaken in accordance with the agreed plan and maintained as such thereafter.

conditions.summary: Biodiversity Net Gain Plan (statutory requirement under Schedule 7A TCPA 1990)
conditions.text: Paragraph 13 of Schedule 7A to the Town and Country Planning Act 1990 states that planning permission is deemed to have been granted subject to the 'biodiversity gain condition' which means development granted by this notice must not begin unless: (a) a Biodiversity Gain Plan has been submitted to the planning authority, and (b) the planning authority has approved the plan. If this permission has the effect of requiring or permitting the development to proceed in phases, then Biodiversity gain plans would be required to be submitted to, and approved by, the planning authority before development may be begun (the overall plan), and before each phase of development may be begun (phase plans).

These details will be retained and maintained as such thereafter.

conditions.summary: Secure covered cycling parking facilities
conditions.text: Prior to the first occupation of the approved accommodation, details of secure covered cycling parking facilities shall be submitted to and approved by the Local Planning Authority. The approved cycle parking facilities shall be permanently retained and maintained for the lifetime of the development.

conditions.summary: Final acoustic assessment and verification report
conditions.text: A final acoustic assessment and verification report completed by a suitably qualified and competent person shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority prior to the first occupation of the approved accommodation. The assessment and report shall verify all mitigation has been implemented and that it provides the mitigation as stated in the acoustic report provided (Spratt and Hamer V2 26/08/2025).

conditions.summary: Management plan for noise and operational control
conditions.text: Prior to the first occupation of the development, a management plan covering the entirety of the use shall be submitted for approval to the local planning authority. The plan shall include but not be limited to examples such as control of noise from plant and machinery, noise from internal and external activities. The plan should include procedures for response to complaints from residents or the local authority. It should include a review mechanism in response to justified complaints. Once approved the plan shall be implemented to the satisfaction of the local planning authority and the use shall only operate in accordance with the approved plan.

conditions.summary: External lighting scheme with ILP compliance
conditions.text: No external lighting shall be installed until a detailed scheme of lighting has been submitted to, and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. This scheme shall take note of and refer to the ILP Guidance Note 01/21 The Reduction Of Obtrusive Light (and any subsequent revisions) and shall include a layout plan with beam orientation and a schedule of light equipment proposed (luminaire type; mounting height; aiming angles and luminaire profiles) and an ISO lux plan showing light spill. The scheme of lighting shall be installed, maintained and operated in accordance with the approved scheme.

conditions.summary: Holiday let use only with occupancy register
conditions.text: The accommodation hereby permitted shall not be occupied as a person's sole or main place of residence, the accommodation shall be occupied for bona fide holiday purposes only and shall accord with the following: (i) The operators of the site shall maintain an up-to-date register of the names, main home addresses and the duration of stay of all future occupants of the approved accommodation. (ii) Relevant contact details (name, position, telephone number, email address and postal address) of the operators of the site, who will keep the register (referred to at (i)) and make it available for inspection, shall also be submitted to the local planning authority (planningenforcement@maidstone.gov.uk) prior to the first occupation of the approved accommodation with the relevant contact details subsequently kept up to date at all times. (iii) The register information required by point (ii) shall be made available at all reasonable times upon request from the local planning authority and additionally at the end of each calendar year following first occupation of the approved accommodation.

conditions.summary: External lighting in accordance with ILP guidance and bat conservation requirements
conditions.text: Any external lighting installed on the site (whether permanent or temporary) shall be in accordance with details that have previously been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The submitted details shall: a) be in accordance with the Institute of Lighting Professionals Guidance Notes for the Reduction of Obtrusive Light, and b) follow the recommendations within the Bat Conservation Trust's 'Guidance Note 8 Bats and Artificial Lighting'. c) include a layout plan with beam orientation and a schedule of light equipment proposed (luminaire type; mounting height; aiming angles and luminaire profiles) and an ISO lux plan showing light spill. d) provide evidence that external lighting has been designed to be the minimum necessary. e) show that external lighting is on timers and on motion sensors. The development shall thereafter be carried out in accordance with the subsequently approved details and retained and maintained as such thereafter.

conditions.summary: Biodiversity Net Gain Plan to be submitted and approved before development begins
conditions.text: Planning permission is deemed to have been granted subject to the 'biodiversity gain condition' which means development granted by this notice must not begin unless: (a) a Biodiversity Gain Plan has been submitted to the planning authority, and (b) the planning authority has approved the plan. There are statutory exemptions and transitional arrangements which mean that the biodiversity gain condition does not always apply.

conditions.summary: Materials in accordance with approved plans and application
conditions.text: The materials to be used in the development hereby approved shall be as indicated on the approved plans and application form (received 04.07.2025).

conditions.summary: Enhancement of ecology on site
conditions.text: The development shall not commence above slab level until details of a scheme for the enhancement of ecology on the site has been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The scheme shall consist of the enhancement of ecology through integrated methods into the fabric of the buildings by means such as swift bricks, bat tubes and bee bricks, and through the provision within the wider application site of measures such as bird and bat boxes, bug hotels, log piles, planting which favours pollinators and hedgehog gaps/corridors. The development shall be implemented in accordance with the approved details prior to the first occupation of the relevant building or for the wider site prior to the first occupation of the last building to be occupied and all features shall be permanently retained and maintained thereafter.

conditions.summary: Soft landscape scheme submission and approval
conditions.text: The development hereby approved shall not commence above slab level until a soft landscape scheme has been submitted to and approved in writing by the local planning authority. The scheme shall (a) be designed in accordance with the principles of the Council's landscape character guidance (Maidstone Landscape Character Assessment Supplement 2012) (b) show all existing trees, hedges and blocks of landscaping on, and immediately adjacent to, the site. (c) provide details of new on-site planting in a planting specification (location, spacing, species, quantity, maturity). (Only non-plastic guards shall be used for the new trees and hedgerows). (d) provide details of proposed hardstanding, including details of material, image samples and manufacturers brochure. (e) provide a [5] year landscape management plan

conditions.summary: Replacement of failed or damaged landscaping
conditions.text: If any of the approved landscaping fails to establish or, within five years of planting, if the landscaping dies, is removed, or becomes so seriously damaged or diseased that long-term amenity value has been adversely affected, the landscaping shall be replaced in the next planting season with plants of the same species and size as detailed in the approved landscape scheme.

conditions.summary: Renewable or low carbon energy production (at least 10% on-site)
conditions.text: The development shall not commence above slab level until details of a scheme to incorporate at least 10% on-site renewable or low carbon energy production measured as a percentage of overall consumption, in accordance with the Energy and Sustainability Statement Rev 1 (received 04.07.2025), has been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. Such details shall include measures for battery energy storage unless this is demonstrated with evidence to be unfeasible. The approved details shall be implemented prior to the first use/occupation of any unit to which the details relate and thereafter retained.

conditions.summary: External lighting in accordance with ILP and Bat Conservation Trust guidance
conditions.text: Any external lighting installed on the site associated with the new buildings (whether permanent or temporary) shall be in accordance with details that have previously been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. a) be in accordance with the Institute of Lighting Professionals Guidance Notes for the Reduction of Obtrusive Light, GN01, dated 2011 (and any subsequent revisions) b) follow the recommendations within the Bat Conservation Trust's 'Guidance Note 8 Bats and Artificial Lighting'. c) include a layout plan with beam orientation and a schedule of light equipment proposed (luminaire type; mounting height; aiming angles and luminaire profiles) and an ISO lux plan showing light spill.

conditions.summary: Tree protection during construction (BS 5837 compliance)
conditions.text: All construction activities and tree protection shall be carried out in accordance with the approved pre-development Arboricultural Assessment Report Rev A prepared by Sylvanarb, dated 26.06.2025 and file reference SA/2351/25-A, Tree Protection Plan prepared by Sylvanarb 16.06.2025, reference FST/TPP/2328-03-A. The development hereby approved shall not commence until tree protection is in place in accordance with the current edition of BS 5837. All trees to be retained must be protected by barriers and/or ground protection. No equipment, plant, machinery or materials shall be brought onto the site prior to the erection of approved barriers and/or ground protection except to carry out pre commencement operations approved in writing by the local planning authority. Nothing shall be stored or placed, nor fires lit, within any of the protected areas. No alterations shall be made to the siting of barriers and/or ground protection, nor ground levels changed, nor excavations made within these areas without the written consent of the local planning authority. These measures shall be maintained until all equipment, machinery and surplus materials have been removed from the site.

conditions.summary: Acoustic assessment for renewable equipment (BS 4142 compliance)
conditions.text: Prior to installation of the renewable equipment (previously approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority through condition 7.) an acoustic assessment and subsequent report shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The acoustic assessment and report shall be completed by a suitably qualified and competent person to demonstrate that the rating level of noise emitted from any plant and equipment to be installed on the site (determined using the guidance of the current version of BS 4142 for rating and assessing industrial and commercial sound) is 5dB below the existing measured background noise level LA90, T. Where the background sound level is below 30dB(A) or where assessment penalties total above 5dB the applicant's consultant shall contact the Environmental Protection Team to agree a site-specific target level.

conditions.summary: Archaeological field evaluation and investigation
conditions.text: Prior to the commencement of development, the applicant, or their agents or successors in title, will secure: i) archaeological field evaluation works in accordance with a specification and written timetable which has been submitted to and approved by the Local Planning Authority; and ii) further archaeological investigation, recording and reporting, determined by the results of the evaluation, in accordance with a specification and timetable which has been submitted to and approved by the Local Planning Authority; iii) programme of post excavation assessment and publication. The development shall only proceed in accordance with the agreed archaeological details.

conditions.summary: Sustainable surface water drainage scheme
conditions.text: Prior to the commencement of development, a detailed sustainable surface water drainage scheme for the site shall be submitted to (and approved in writing by) the local planning authority. The submitted scheme shall demonstrate compliance with the required technical standards at the time of submission and shall demonstrate that the surface water generated by this development (for all rainfall durations and intensities up to and including the climate change adjusted critical 100 year storm) can be accommodated and disposed of within the curtilage of the site without increase to flood risk on or offsite. The drainage scheme shall also demonstrate (with reference to published guidance): i) that silt and pollutants resulting from the site use can be adequately managed to ensure there is no pollution risk to receiving waters. ii) appropriate operational, maintenance and access requirements for each drainage feature or SuDS component are adequately considered, including any proposed arrangements for future adoption by any public body or statutory undertaker. The drainage scheme shall be implemented in accordance with the approved details prior to occupation of the development hereby approved.

conditions.summary: Verification report for surface water drainage system
conditions.text: Prior to the first occupation of the development a Verification Report, pertaining to the surface water drainage system and prepared by a suitably competent person, shall have been submitted to and approved by the Local Planning Authority. The Report shall demonstrate that the drainage system constructed is consistent with that which was approved. The Report shall contain information and evidence (including photographs) of details and locations of inlets, outlets and control structures; landscape plans; full as built drawings; information pertinent to the installation of those items identified on the critical drainage assets drawing; and, the submission of an operation and maintenance manual for the sustainable drainage scheme as constructed.

conditions.summary: Parking and turning areas protection
conditions.text: No development, whether permitted by the Town and Country Planning (General Permitted Development) (England ) Order 2015 (or any order revoking and re-enacting that Order, with or without modification) or not, shall be carried out on the parking and turning areas indicated on the approved plans or in such a position as to preclude vehicular access to them.

conditions.summary: BREEAM Very Good rating (UK New Construction V6.1)
conditions.text: The buildings hereby approved shall achieve a Very Good BREEAM UK New Construction Version 6.1 rating including maximising energy and water efficiencies under the mandatory energy and water credits. A final certificate shall be issued to the Local Planning Authority for approval in writing within 6 months of the first occupation of the relevant building to certify that at a Very Good BREEAM UK New Construction Version 6.1 rating has been achieved.

conditions.summary: Community use agreement for dual use of facilities
conditions.text: Prior to the first occupation of the development, a community use agreement shall be submitted to and approved by the local planning authority. The community use agreement shall set out measures to secure access to the facilities by the wider community outside the normal school day. The facilities shall thereafter be made available in accordance with the approved agreement.

conditions.summary: Habitat Management and Monitoring Plan (30-year period)
conditions.text: No development shall take place until a Habitat Management and Monitoring Plan (HMMP) has been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The HMMP shall show how the minimum 10% onsite biodiversity net gain (submitted and approved through the Biodiversity Gain Plan) for a period of 30 years from completion of the development will be maintained and the HMMP shall include: (i)a non-technical summary; (ii)the roles and responsibilities of the people or organisation(s) delivering the HMMP; (iii)the planned habitat creation and enhancement works to create or improve habitat to achieve the biodiversity net gain in accordance with the approved Biodiversity Gain Plan; (iv)the management measures to maintain habitat in accordance with the approved Biodiversity Gain Plan for a period of 30 years from the completion of development; and (v) the monitoring methodology and frequency in respect of the created or enhanced habitat to be submitted to the local planning authority. The development shall be implemented in full accordance with the requirements of the approved HMMP.

(ii) details of a native landscaping scheme (designed in accordance with the submitted details and the principles of Council's Landscape Character Guidance and Landscape Character Assessment Supplement 2012), to include the planting of new landscaping to reduce the negative visual impact of the large area of hardstanding that currently forms the building setting. (vi) a low wall with railings and a privet hedge along the site frontage and replacement of existing coping on the side boundary wall with ragstone coping; and (vii) a timetable for implementation of the Site Development Scheme. (b) If within 11 months of the date of this decision the local planning authority refuse to approve the Site Development Scheme or fail to give a decision within the prescribed period, an appeal shall have been made to, and accepted as validly made by, the Secretary of State. (c) If an appeal is made in pursuance of above, that appeal shall have been finally determined and submitted Site Development Scheme shall have been approved by Secretary of State. Upon implementation of the approved Site Development Scheme specified in this condition, that Scheme shall thereafter be maintained/retained.

conditions.summary: Landscape scheme design requirements and specifications

Within five years from planting, any landscaping which is removed, fails to establish, dies or become so seriously damaged or diseased that their long term amenity value has been adversely affected shall be replaced in the next planting season with plants of the same species and size as detailed in the approved landscape scheme unless the local planning authority gives written consent to any variation.

conditions.summary: Biodiversity Net Gain Plan submission and approval
conditions.text: Paragraph 13 of Schedule 7A to the Town and Country Planning Act 1990 states that planning permission is deemed to have been granted subject to the "biodiversity gain condition" which means development granted by this notice must not begin unless: (a) a Biodiversity Gain Plan has been submitted to the planning authority, and (b) the planning authority has approved the plan. There are statutory exemptions and transitional arrangements which mean that the biodiversity gain condition does not always apply.

conditions.summary: Commencement within three years

conditions.summary: Occupation by Gypsies and Travellers only

The plan shall show the type and locations of external lighting, as well as the expected light spill in lux levels, to demonstrate that areas to be lit shall not adversely impact biodiversity. All external lighting shall be installed in accordance with the specifications and locations set out in the plan and shall be maintained thereafter.
